Decision briefing: sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB), obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D)

For the Group of Secretaries (Environment, Health, Finance, Science and Technology, PMO). Prepared by NITI Aayog. Data as queried on 2026-10-23 (export date). Tags: [c#] = data query run for this briefing, [r#] = References, (est.) = estimate from memory.

1. Verdict

Measured.

  • Research: 283 typed papers (2017 to 2025) and 297 abstract-bearing title-anchored papers (1990 to 2025) on the exposure; 11,867 the health literature index records on the subject [c3]. Top-tier evidence read: one meta-analysis [r1] and one systematic review [r2].

Connected argument 2. India is studied more than it is reported. It ranks fifth in first-author output (421 papers) [c5] but has a news lift of only 0.4 [c8], and it sits outside the top twelve journal countries [c5]. Connected argument 3. The causal chain is thin where we need it: 283 papers on the exposure, 63,944 on the outcome, and only 3 on both by title [c3]. The strong estimates come from meta-analytic pooling [r1][r2], not from this title overlap.
